_comment: Per-crate line-coverage floors, in percent. Seeded at what each crate actually measured when this file was created (#98) -- a floor that started above today's coverage would fail on day one for no reason, so this is a ratchet: raising a floor is a deliberate commit, never the seed. Only the pure/logic crates CLAUDE.md calls out get a floor: scripts/coverage.sh only ever measures the crates listed here. A crate like postio-gtk, whose tests need a compositor, is deliberately left out rather than given a low floor -- a single global number across crates this different is exactly the vanity metric #98 exists to avoid. Re-baselined 2026-09-01 (#781): postio-model measured 94.25% against a 95.0 floor, postio-search 95.90% against 96.5, and postio-sync 88.15% against 89.0 -- drift that accumulated while CI was dispatch-only and nothing was measuring. postio-sync's was invisible at first: the run crashed on an earlier crate and never reached it. Lowered to the next 0.5 below what they measure, deliberately and in the open, so the ratchet starts catching drift again from where the code actually is. #784 won postio-model and postio-search back to their pre-#781 floors: 95.80% and 99.09% now measured against 95.0 and 96.5, comfortable headroom rather than a razor's edge, added by covering real behaviour a floor number alone would not have justified (a case-insensitive Ord/Hash contract, a filter-to-field mapping checked one variant at a time, a couple of accessors nothing called) -- not by raising the floors to match what was measured. postio-sync stayed at #781's lowered floor until #997, which won it back too: 89.20% now measured against 89.0, by covering real branches a floor number alone would not have justified in cross_account.rs's copy/remove sagas (a search or upload failure backing off rather than failing outright, a replay against an already-aborted saga, a removal with no server coordinate anywhere settling without contacting a server, a copy racing ahead of its own blob backfill), blob_sink.rs's own error paths (a chunk after finish, a finish after finish, a genuine storage failure surfacing as a fetch failure), and discover.rs's link_parents/DiscoveryReport (a missing intermediate hierarchy level, a stable second pass, and the accessors nothing had called).
